blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Make fsck_report(recover=True) return the recover run's actual output instead of running recover narrative through the scan-only _transform_json.
evidence: src/rebar/_lib_reads.py:387: `raw = _fsck_mod._transform_json(out.getvalue())`
_transform_json parses only lines matching `^([A-Z_]+):\s*(.*)$` (src/rebar/_commands/fsck.py:124), designed for scan `KIND:` lines

fsck_recover_cli emits narrative text, e.g. src/rebar/_commands/fsck_recover.py:246 `"Recovery successful: rebase drained via --continue"`, :286 `"No dangling ticket commits found"`, :324 `f"Recovery complete: {recovered_count} commits cherry-picked"` — none in KIND: form
Old contract returned the recover text verbatim: src/rebar/_lib_reads.py:334 `return _out.getvalue()`
blocking.finding: fsck_report(recover=True) feeds fsck_recover_cli's plain-English narrative output through _transform_json, which only parses scan-style `KIND:` lines — so the recover path yields an empty/garbage issues[] rather than the recovery narrative the old fsck(recover=True) returned.
scenarios: A client calls the MCP fsck tool with recover=True on a writable server and receives an empty issues[] despite recovery running
